messages:
Anya Patel: Quick heads-up — I'm putting together a combined PRD + runtime RFC for kernel selection, attention optimizations, and updated KV cache policies. This is driven by 3 mid-size customers asking for deterministic fallbacks, tighter p99 memory, and safer quantization defaults. Want to align on scope and launch criteria for H1. Kickoff sync Monday?

Mike Chen: +1. Can you paste baseline perf / mem numbers for the affected models? Also need to decide rollout granularity: by model family (e.g., L2/L3), by shape (seq_len), or by customer.

Sara Gomez: Customer bug: quantized L7 with 8k context saw quality regressions and >10% token-time increase in a few queries. For acceptance criteria I suggest: max 5% quality regression on our eval suite and no >10% p99 latency regression versus current baseline.

Dave Li: Operational note — when KV cache eviction happens under memory pressure we currently see transient 503 spikes. Any policy change must include a recovery SLA (eg: <0.1% increase in error rate during the event) and a graceful fallback path.

Olivia Park: Console/UX ask: we need visible variant labels and simple rollout toggles for operators. I put mockups in Confluence: https://redwood.atl/confluence/ENG-RUNTIME/variant-rollout (will add to PRD).

Anya Patel: Draft acceptance criteria I'm going to propose in the PRD:
```
1) Functional: No more than 5% drop in eval score (instruction-following & summarization suites) after kernel/quant changes.
2) Latency: p50/p95 within 10% of current baseline; p99 not to exceed 1.5x baseline except during controlled canary windows.
3) Reliability: during cache eviction events, customer-facing error-rate increase <= 0.1 percentage points.
4) Compatibility: fallback kernels available when model ABI/version mismatch is detected; detection latency < 50ms.
5) Observability: per-variant metrics in Console (latency, cost-per-token, error-rate) with 1m resolution and alerting hooks.
6) Rollout: canary cohorts support per-customer pinning + automatic rollback on defined regression signals.
```

Mike Chen: Edge cases / technical risks to call out: mixed-precision across batch boundaries, heterogenous GPU fleet capabilities (some nodes lack new kernels), and KV cache consistency during model switchovers. Suggest a simple priority algorithm for runtime kernel selection to include in RFC:
```
select_kernel(request):
  candidates = kernels.supporting(model, dtype, seq_len)
  sort by [compatibility_score, expected_latency, memory_cost, quant_fidelity]
  for k in candidates:
    if k.compatible_with_instance(instance): return k
  return safe_fallback_kernel
```
Note: compatibility_score includes whether kernel has been validated for this model+quant config.

Sara Gomez: For evaluations, we will add regression buckets: retrieval QA, instruction-following, summarization, and long-context coherency. I'll add dataset pointers to the PRD and a baseline job in CI. Also propose a small human eval for any kernel that changes tokenization or sampling.

Dave Li: From SRE side: propose circuit-breaker thresholds and automated rollback triggers: 5% sustained latency increase for 10m or 0.2 percentage-point error-rate increase for 5m. We should also simulate KV-thrash in staging to validate eviction policy.

Anya Patel: Nice. Action items I have: 1) I'll drop a PRD + RFC skeleton by EOD Friday. 2) Mike — fill in kernel selection pseudocode and perf budget. 3) Sara — list eval suites and thresholds. 4) Dave — define SRE rollback thresholds and test plan. 5) Olivia — add Console mocks and minimal API surface for rollout controls. Meeting: Monday 10:00am PT to triage scope and pick canary targets. :calendar: @Mike Chen @Sara Gomez @Dave Li @Olivia Park

infra-bot: Reminder — RFC template available at /docs/rfcs/runtime-kernel-selection-template.md. Please link PRD to the RFC and mark initial PRD as WIP.

Mike Chen: One more note — we should identify 2 low-risk customers for early canary (high observability, tolerant traffic). I'll DM potential candidates after the meeting. :+1:

Anya Patel: Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll create the thread in the RFC PR and tag the document owners.
